newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 15.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Tuesday.

- Ireland's Minister for Education has launched the long-awaited parents' information booklet on the Relationships and Sexuality Education programme, which will become a part of the school curriculum throughout in September.
- At the launch of his party's election manifesto in Belfast on Monday, Sinn Fein president Gerry Adams said it was the most important election since 1918.
- The 1998 World Equestrian Games will not be held at the Royal Dublin Society showgrounds at Ballsbridge.
- Members of the Bristol and West Building Society will vote on Tuesday on the 600 million Irish pound takeover of the society by Bank of Ireland.
- The Irish government was under intense pressure on Monday to explain how a triple killer wanted in Britain since 1981 could claim social welfare and work on a state-sponsored course in Ireland.
- Local authorities around Ireland are keeping a close eye on water supplies as the long dry spell sees reservoir levels fall to worrying levels.
- A report by the Dublin Chamber of Commerce shows many small companies failing to keep up with some of the advances in technology, although use of the Internet looks set to grow.
- Irish fishermen face massive fleet cuts under a deal expected to emerge during EU talks in Luxembourg on Tuesday.

- Irish small and medium-sized companies were warned to be on the alert for a number of British-based operators offering advice on EU grant applications and promising funding in return for an up-front fee.
